findings.passage: "I think it's just another day in the regressive era where we're taking that back and rolling back the ability of people to access the polls," said State Senator Chris Larson.
findings.note: Quoted by CBS58 after the US Supreme Court declined to hear an appeal of Wisconsin's photo ID law.

findings.passage: " Its just simply adding another layer for people to get to the polls. That's it.The in-person voter fraud is so rare. It's a fraction of a percent," said Larson.
findings.note: Quoted by CBS58 on the photo ID requirement and the rarity of in-person voter fraud.

findings.passage: “A violation of the spirit of democracy, this legislation disproportionately affects the elderly, disabled, and indefinitely confined, mandating onerous applications and status checks.
findings.note: Press release statement from Sen. Larson on the other caucus absentee-voting bills passed that day (date inferred from the page's reference to the 102nd anniversary of the state ratifying women's suffrage; exact day unknown).
